question: In the lithium-mediated ammonia review's comparison of electrolysers, what is the mean faradaic efficiency of the gas diffusion electrode flow cells?
trap: including the MEA reactor (9%) or the Pd membrane (36%)
rendered:
According to Table 1 on page 9, there are three entries for gas diffusion electrode (GDE) flow cells. 

- Conguration: GDE ow cell | Electrolyte: LiBF4 C2H5OH/ THF | Current density/ mA cm^−2: −8.8 | Faradaic efficiency/%: 35 | Yield rate/ nmol s^−1 cm^−2: 24 | Stability/ hour: 2 | Energy efficiency/%: — | Limitations: High cell voltage, solvent oxidation
- Conguration: GDE ow cell | Electrolyte: LiBF4 C2H5OH/ THF | Current density/ mA cm^−2: −6 | Faradaic efficiency/%: 61 | Yield rate/ nmol s^−1 cm^−2: 4 | Stability/ hour: 13 | Energy efficiency/%: 13 | Limitations: Solvent cost
- Conguration: GDE ow cell | Electrolyte: LiBF4 C2H5OH/ DG | Current density/ mA cm^−2: −6 | Faradaic efficiency/%: 64 | Yield rate/ nmol s^−1 cm^−2: 10 | Stability/ hour: 17 | Energy efficiency/%: — | Limitations: Solvent cost DG

The mean faradaic efficiency of the gas diffusion electrode flow cells is (35 + 61 + 64)/3 = 53.33%.
